name: Gazetteer Named Place Ingest Nodes
description: The ORCHESTRATION half of the GeoNames gazetteer lane. geonames-source is the request-scoped decoder - dump in, $GNP stream out, capabilities [], nothing persisted - which is the right shape for a browser and the wrong shape for a scheduled ingest, and the two cannot be one plugin. The ingest-only decisions live here, mirroring the cell-tower-source / cell-tower-ingest split exactly: four pure nodes read a durable resume mark, decide seed vs daily delta vs ledgered no-op, author the storage attribution, and advance the mark only from a verified store. The mark DOUBLES AS THE SAME-DATA LEDGER: the upstream ETag and Last-Modified ride on it, and a tick whose HEAD/GET matches the mark is a no-op that costs one conditional request. NO CAPABILITIES: http, storage and flatsql are the generic hostcap connector nodes, so this plugin performs no I/O and needs no new host connector.

sequentialJustification.detail: All four methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: they format a query, a set of fetch descriptors, an attribution frame or a mark. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Turns the daily timer tick into the flatsql-query that reads this dataset's resume mark back. It is a SEPARATE node from ingest_plan on purpose: the plan takes the mark as an INPUT, and a node that emitted its own input would be a cycle in the flow graph. It emits {"sql","params"} and not {"table","where"}, because hostcap/flatsql-query's query reads sql and returns 400 missing-sql for anything else. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.description: ONE TICK IS ONE BOUNDED UNIT OF WORK. The first tick fetches the SEED archive plus the three lookup files; every later tick fetches that day's modifications and deletes, which are full geoname rows and so upsert through the same decoder. A tick whose upstream ETag matches the one on the mark emits NOTHING and the run ends without a fetch - the same-data ledger is the mark itself, not a second store. The seed fetch carries a Range header bounded by the Go host's 4 MiB response-body cap (hostcap/http-request manifest): a larger body is TRUNCATED by the host and inflates to a plausible short gazetteer with no error anywhere, so the plan asks for exactly what it can receive and ingest_meta refuses the run if Content-Range proves the object is larger. Fails closed with no configured base URL rather than inventing one. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.description: Authors the attribution the storage lane cannot invent - dataset, source, batch and the $GNP.SOURCE dataset provenance - and forwards the records untouched. It takes the http response because the ETag, Last-Modified and Content-Range TOTAL are only knowable here: the guest that dispatched the fetch never sees the reply, and Content-Length on a 206 describes the CHUNK, so reading it as the total would end a seed after one chunk with every later byte silently unfetched. The seed uses reconcile=append and the delta uses it too, because a daily modifications file is an UPSERT of a few thousand rows and not the gazetteer's complete set - reconciling on it would delete the entire rest of the world. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. methods.description: Advances the resume mark from the STORAGE RESULT, never at dispatch: a mark advanced when an edition is requested turns a crash between fetch and store into a permanently skipped day, invisibly. It catches the silent nop that survives hostcap/storage-ingest's own ok:false check - ok:true with inserted=0 for a tick that carried records, byte-identical to a day on which the gazetteer changed nothing - and refuses to advance the mark or the ledgered ETag over rows that were never stored. The epoch announce is the node's normal publication path (DATASET_EPOCH and DATASET_CID already ride in $GNP.SOURCE, so no new record type is minted); the mark is NOT gated on the publish URL, because a node that stores without publishing must still make progress, and publication itself is fail-closed. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed.
